earlier_scan.note: Sharma's Kinnaur sketches plausibly state stress; print-only, not found online

sources.citation: Österreichische Akademie der Wissenschaften, Phonogrammarchiv. Project page 'Researching and Documenting Endangered Languages of Kinnaur' (contact Christian Huber), Wayback 2026-01-03.
sources.note: States that systematic research on 'Shumcho/Humcho, Jangrami (both West Himalayish)' began 2001-2004 and that 'Jangrami (Ethnologue: Jangshung) is the language of the high caste in Jangi, Lippa and Asrang'; the publication list (Huber 2007, 2011, 2013, 2014, 2017 PhD, 2019, 2023) is entirely on Shumcho — no Jangshung publication.
Only vitality/location data from Ethnologue 16, UNESCO Atlas 2010, WALS and the World Oral Literature Project; no bibliography of descriptions.

sources.citation: Saxena, Anju (ed.). 2022. The Linguistic Landscape of the Indian Himalayas: Languages in Kinnaur (Brill's Studies in South and Southwest Asian Languages 14). Leiden: Brill (open access).
sources.note: Stress statements concern Kinnauri (Sangla) and Kinnauri Pahari only. Jangshung appears once, in Table 50 (p. 407) reproducing Ethnologue's list ('Jangshung (jna) Jangrami, Zangram, Zhang-Zhung, Jangiam, Thebor... / Jangi, Lippa, Asrang (Morang)'); the lexical survey villages (Sangla, Nichar, Kalpa, Ropa, Chitkul, Labrang, Poo, Kuno, Nako) include no Jangshung village.

sources.citation: Sharma, Devidatta (D.D.). 1989. Tribal Languages of Himachal Pradesh, Part I (Studies in Tibeto-Himalayan Languages 2). Delhi: Mittal Publications.
sources.note: Covers Pattani, Tinani, Gahri and Tod (Lahaul) only; accent sections for those languages (e.g. p. 34 Pattani initial-syllable accent, p. 202 Gahri). No Jangrami/Jangshung anywhere in the text layer (0 hits for jangram/jangi/lippa/asrang).
No descriptive (grammar/sketch/phonology) references; only overviews, comparative works and Ethnologue/UNESCO entries. Alternative names include Jangrami, Thebarskad, Thebor, Zhang-Zhung.
No linguistic description; cites only ELP, Negi 2012 (sociolinguistic profile, Nepalese Linguistics 27) and the OeAW project page.

sources.citation: OLAC, 'OLAC resources in and about the Jangshung language' (jna), as of 2023-09-26.
sources.note: The only 'language descriptions' listed are Rosetta Project excerpts of Haarh 1968, The Zhang-Zhung Language (the extinct Old Zhangzhung of Bon texts), mis-mapped to jna; nothing on Jangshung proper.

sources.citation: Huber, Christian. 2007. Researching local languages in Kinnaur. In J. Ahamer & G. Lechleitner (eds.), Um-Feld-Forschung: Erfahrungen – Erlebnisse – Ergebnisse, 249-266. Wien: Verlag der Österreichischen Akademie der Wissenschaften.
sources.note: Nothing on stress. p. 254: 'To date no study is available of any of the Thebarskad (or Indo-European lower caste language) varieties... Published data from the high caste language of Jangi, Lippa and Asrang is perhaps confined to the words collected in the Lippa entries of J. D. Cunningham's (1844: 225ff.) list of Thebarskad ("Tibberkad") words.' p. 256: the Jangi/Lippa/Asrang high-caste language = Ethnologue's Jangshung, 'not to be confused with the extinct Zhangzhung language'. p. 263: the OeAW project assembled a Jangshung vocabulary and texts, but publication focus was Shumcho.

sources.citation: Sharma, Devidatta (D.D.). 1988. A Descriptive Grammar of Kinnauri (Studies in Tibeto-Himalayan Languages 1). Delhi: Mittal Publications.
sources.note: Describes Standard (Lower) Kinnauri only. p. 6 lists 'II. Thebarskad' as a dialect group 'in villages Lippa, Jangi, Asrang, Labang, Kanam, Sunnam, Namgya and Shaso' (i.e. Jangshung + Shumcho + Sunnam) with no data. pp. 45-46 '(v) Stress and Pitch': 'Kinnauri neither, like English, is a stressed language, nor, like Chinese, a tonal one... Usually in a polysyllabic word the initial syllable has a higher stress and the non-initial a higher pitch. Being non-phonemic these features... can occur in free variation' — a statement about Kinnauri (kinn1249, already in catalog), not about Jangshung.

sources.citation: Language Division, Office of the Registrar General, India. [2010s]. Linguistic Survey of India: Himachal Pradesh (Kinnauri chapter by P. Perumal Samy).
sources.note: Kinnauri sketch only; no mention of Jangrami/Jangshung/Thebarskad/Jangi/Lippa (0 hits).

sources.citation: Sharma, Devidatta (D.D.). 1992. Tribal Languages of Himachal Pradesh, Part II (Studies in Tibeto-Himalayan Languages 3). Delhi: Mittal Publications (1996 reissue 414 pp., ISBN 8170991021).

sources.note: Named by the earlier scan as containing a Jangrami sketch. Bibliographic evidence from opened sources says otherwise: its sketches are Nyamkad (Kinnauri Bhoti), Chhitkuli (pp. 197-304) and Kanashi (pp. 305-399), and Huber 2007 (who cites it) states no study of any Thebarskad variety exists. Listed only so the lead can be closed by a page check of its table of contents.

sources.citation: Huber, Christian (Phonogrammarchiv, Österreichische Akademie der Wissenschaften). Unpublished Jangshung/Jangrami field materials (vocabulary, glossed texts, songs, sound recordings) from the FWF project P15046 (2001-2004) and 2007 fieldwork in Jangi.
sources.tag: wanted: likely states stress, not held
sources.note: Per Huber 2007 p. 263 and the OeAW project page these are the only modern first-hand data on Jangshung ('perhaps the first phonographic evidence'); Huber is the one person who could state where stress falls. A direct enquiry is the realistic route.

sources.citation: Chamberlain, Wendy, Brad Chamberlain & Emma Pavey. 1998. A Sociolinguistic Survey of Kinnauri spoken in Kinnaur District, Himachal Pradesh, India. 79 pp. SIL survey manuscript.

sources.note: The only survey-era document that sampled the Jangshung villages (source of Ethnologue's 1,990 speakers); SIL survey reports usually contain wordlists, sometimes with stress marked, rarely a prose stress statement.
